chunks.content:
1. INTRODUCTION & EARTHWORM SPECIES SELECTION
Vermicomposting is the biological degradation and stabilization of organic waste through earthworm activity, yielding nutrient-rich organic manure. For tropical and sub-tropical Indian agro-climatic conditions, the two scientifically validated epigeic earthworm species are:
- Eisenia fetida (Red Californian Earthworm): Highly prolific, tolerates temperatures between 18°C and 35°C, moisture tolerance of 60-70%, and high digestion efficiency of cow dung and crop biomass.
- Eudrilus eugeniae (African Nightcrawler): Larger biomass turnover, ideal for southern and central Indian humid zones.

metadata.title: ICAR-CRIDA: Scientific Protocol for Commercial and Farm-Scale Vermicomposting
metadata.author: Central Research Institute for Dryland Agriculture (ICAR-CRIDA), Hyderabad

chunks.content:
2. PIT AND BED DESIGN SPECIFICATIONS
- Dimensions: Length 10 to 30 feet, width 3 to 4 feet, depth/height 2 to 2.5 feet. Beds exceeding 4 feet width hinder center aeration and worm movement.
- Flooring: Compacted clay floor or loose brick lining with a slight slope (2%) towards an outlet channel to collect nutrient-dense vermiwash. Avoid pure concrete flooring without drainage.
- Thatched Roof: Essential thatched roofing made of coconut fronds, bamboo, or agri-shade nets (75% shade) to prevent direct solar radiation and rain saturation.

metadata.title: ICAR-CRIDA: Scientific Protocol for Commercial and Farm-Scale Vermicomposting
metadata.author: Central Research Institute for Dryland Agriculture (ICAR-CRIDA), Hyderabad

chunks.content:
3. FEEDSTOCK AND PRE-DECOMPOSITION PROTOCOL
Raw animal dung must NEVER be fed directly to earthworms due to heat release during thermophilic decomposition (>55°C) and harmful gases.
- Ratio: 60% cow dung or farmyard manure mixed with 40% chopped dry crop biomass (paddy straw, maize stover, pulses husk, dried tree leaves).
- Pre-digestion: Heap the biomass and dung mixture, sprinkle water, and let it undergo partial thermophilic aerobic decomposition for 15 to 20 days with one turning at day 10. Once temperature cools below 30°C, transfer into vermi-beds.

metadata.title: ICAR-CRIDA: Scientific Protocol for Commercial and Farm-Scale Vermicomposting
metadata.author: Central Research Institute for Dryland Agriculture (ICAR-CRIDA), Hyderabad

chunks.content:
4. INOCULATION AND BED MAINTENANCE
- Inoculation Rate: Introduce 1.5 to 2 kg healthy earthworms (approx. 1,500 to 2,000 worms) per square meter or 10 kg per standard 20x3x2 ft bed.
- Moisture Management: Maintain 60% to 70% moisture consistently by sprinkling water every 2 to 3 days depending on season. Moisture test: Take a fistful of bed material; squeezing firmly should produce 2-3 drops of water without slurry dripping.
- Aeration: Loosen the top 2-3 inches gently using a wooden fork once every fortnight.

metadata.title: ICAR-CRIDA: Scientific Protocol for Commercial and Farm-Scale Vermicomposting
metadata.author: Central Research Institute for Dryland Agriculture (ICAR-CRIDA), Hyderabad

chunks.content:
5. HARVESTING AND POST-HARVEST SIFTING
- Cycle Duration: 45 to 60 days per batch. The surface will show uniform dark brown, granular, tea-leaf-like casting aggregates.
- Harvesting Technique: Cease watering 4-5 days prior to harvest. The earthworms migrate to the moist lower bottom layers. Scrape top 6 inches of vermicompost. Heap the harvest in small cones in shade; remaining worms move downwards, allowing pure castings to be separated.
- Sieving: Pass through a 3 mm wire mesh sieve. Air-dry under shade to 20% moisture before bagging in HDPE bags.

metadata.title: ICAR-CRIDA: Scientific Protocol for Commercial and Farm-Scale Vermicomposting
metadata.author: Central Research Institute for Dryland Agriculture (ICAR-CRIDA), Hyderabad

chunks.content:
6. NUTRIENT PROFILE AND FIELD APPLICATION DOSAGE
- Chemical Composition: Organic Carbon: 14-18%, Available Nitrogen (N): 1.6-2.2%, Available Phosphorus (P2O5): 1.2-1.8%, Available Potassium (K2O): 1.5-2.4%, C:N Ratio: 12:1 to 15:1. Rich in humic acid, fulvic acid, phosphatase, and indole acetic acid (IAA).
- Dosage Guidelines:
  * Field crops (Paddy, Wheat, Maize): 2.0 to 2.5 tonnes per acre incorporated during final land preparation.
  * Pulses and Oilseeds: 1.5 tonnes per acre as basal manure.
  * Commercial Vegetables (Tomato, Chilli, Brinjal, Onion): 3.0 tonnes per acre, applied in planting furrows.

metadata.title: ICAR-CRIDA: Scientific Protocol for Commercial and Farm-Scale Vermicomposting
metadata.author: Central Research Institute for Dryland Agriculture (ICAR-CRIDA), Hyderabad

chunks.content:
* Commercial Vegetables (Tomato, Chilli, Brinjal, Onion): 3.0 tonnes per acre, applied in planting furrows.
  * Fruit Orchards (Mango, Citrus, Pomegranate, Guava): 5 to 10 kg per mature tree around the drip line ring twice annually (pre-monsoon and post-monsoon).

metadata.title: ICAR-CRIDA: Scientific Protocol for Commercial and Farm-Scale Vermicomposting
metadata.author: Central Research Institute for Dryland Agriculture (ICAR-CRIDA), Hyderabad

chunks.content:
1. PRINCIPLE AND SCIENTIFIC BASIS
Jeevamrutham is a fermented liquid microbial consortium prepared from indigenous (Desi) cow dung, urine, pulses flour, jaggery, and living farm soil. It acts not merely as a direct chemical N-P-K fertilizer, but primarily as a catalytic microbial inoculant that multiplies beneficial soil bacteria (rhizobacteria, phosphate solubilizers, actinomycetes) and accelerates soil organic carbon mineralization.

metadata.title: National Centre for Organic and Natural Farming: Standardized Preparation Protocol for Jeevamrutham
metadata.author: National Centre for Organic and Natural Farming (NCONF), Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Ghaziabad

chunks.content:
2. INGREDIENTS PER 200 LITERS (FOR 1 ACRE FIELD APPLICATION)
- Fresh Desi Cow Dung (Bos indicus): 10 kg (rich in cellulolytic and lignolytic gut microflora).
- Fresh Desi Cow Urine (Gomutra): 5 to 10 liters (provides natural urea, minerals, and antimicrobial phenolic compounds).
- Jaggery (Gur) or sugarcane juice: 2 kg organic unrefined jaggery (or 4 liters fresh sugarcane juice) as rapid energy carbon source for bacteria.
- Pulse/Gram Flour (Besan, Blackgram, Greengram, or Cowpea flour): 2 kg (provides essential protein and amino acids).
- Virgin Living Soil: A fistful (approx. 100-200 grams) of soil collected from undisturbed field borders, tree shade, or forest root zones teeming with native mycorrhizae and beneficial microbes.

metadata.title: National Centre for Organic and Natural Farming: Standardized Preparation Protocol for Jeevamrutham
metadata.author: National Centre for Organic and Natural Farming (NCONF), Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Ghaziabad

chunks.content: - Clean Water: 200 liters (free from synthetic chlorination).

metadata.title: National Centre for Organic and Natural Farming: Standardized Preparation Protocol for Jeevamrutham
metadata.author: National Centre for Organic and Natural Farming (NCONF), Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Ghaziabad

chunks.content:
- Clean Water: 200 liters (free from synthetic chlorination).

3. STEP-BY-STEP PREPARATION METHOD
- Container: Use a 200-liter food-grade plastic drum or traditional cement tank placed under tree shade or sheltered roof. Avoid metallic zinc/copper vessels.
- Mixing:
  Step 1: In a bucket, thoroughly mix 10 kg cow dung and 10 liters cow urine with 10 liters water to form a smooth lump-free slurry.
  Step 2: In another bucket, dissolve 2 kg jaggery in 5 liters warm water.
  Step 3: Mix 2 kg pulse flour with 5 liters water without forming lumps.
  Step 4: Pour the dung-urine slurry, jaggery syrup, pulse flour suspension, and fistful of living soil into the 200-liter drum.
  Step 5: Fill the drum with remaining water up to 200 liters. Stir clockwise with a clean wooden pole for 5 minutes.

metadata.title: National Centre for Organic and Natural Farming: Standardized Preparation Protocol for Jeevamrutham
metadata.author: National Centre for Organic and Natural Farming (NCONF), Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Ghaziabad

chunks.content:
Step 5: Fill the drum with remaining water up to 200 liters. Stir clockwise with a clean wooden pole for 5 minutes.
- Incubation and Fermentation:
  * Cover drum mouth with breathable jute bag or porous cotton cloth to allow gas escape and prevent housefly egg-laying.
  * Keep in complete shade for 48 to 72 hours.
  * Stir the mixture clockwise for 5 minutes twice daily (morning and evening).
  * Peak microbial colony forming units (>10^9 CFU/ml) are reached between 48 to 96 hours.

metadata.title: National Centre for Organic and Natural Farming: Standardized Preparation Protocol for Jeevamrutham
metadata.author: National Centre for Organic and Natural Farming (NCONF), Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Ghaziabad

chunks.content:
4. METHODS OF APPLICATION AND TIMING
- Flood Irrigation Application: Pour the 200 liters of fermented Jeevamrutham at the main water inlet channel of the field so it disperses uniformly with irrigation water across 1 acre.
- Drip Irrigation Fertigation: Filter the liquid through a two-stage filter: first through fine nylon/muslin cloth, then through sand/screen drip filters to eliminate organic particulate blockage.
- Foliar Spray: Filter liquid meticulously through fine double muslin cloth. Dilute 10 liters of Jeevamrutham in 100 liters of water (10% concentration) per acre. Spray every 15 to 20 days on crop canopy.
- Frequency: Apply once every 21 days during the vegetative and flowering stages for sustained microbial activity.

metadata.title: National Centre for Organic and Natural Farming: Standardized Preparation Protocol for Jeevamrutham
metadata.author: National Centre for Organic and Natural Farming (NCONF), Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Ghaziabad

chunks.content:
5. PRECAUTIONARY GUIDELINES
- Jeevamrutham has an effective bio-active window of 7 to 8 days post-fermentation. Do not store beyond 10 days as anaerobic acidifying bacteria take over and efficacy drops.
- Always prepare under shade; direct exposure to scorching sunlight destroys microbial strains.

metadata.title: National Centre for Organic and Natural Farming: Standardized Preparation Protocol for Jeevamrutham
metadata.author: National Centre for Organic and Natural Farming (NCONF), Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Ghaziabad

chunks.content:
1. OVERVIEW AND COMPOSITION
Panchagavya is an organic formulation combining five products derived from the indigenous cow along with natural catalysts. It contains rich populations of lactic acid bacteria, yeast, actinomycetes, photosynthetic bacteria, and plant growth-promoting hormones (auxins, gibberellins, and cytokinins).

metadata.title: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU): Agronomic Efficacy and Preparation of Panchagavya
metadata.author: Department of Sustainable Organic Agriculture, TNAU, Coimbatore

chunks.content:
2. REQUIRED INGREDIENTS
- Fresh Cow Dung: 5 kg
- Cow Ghee: 1 kg (or 500 grams desi cow ghee)
- Fresh Cow Urine: 3 liters
- Fresh Cow Milk: 2 liters
- Fresh Cow Curd: 2 liters
- Tender Coconut Water: 3 liters (potent source of natural kinetin and cytokinins)
- Sugarcane Juice or Jaggery: 1 kg jaggery dissolved in 3 liters water
- Ripe Poovan / Desi Bananas: 12 fruits (mashed well)
- Toddy or Fermented Tender Coconut Water (optional accelerator): 2 liters

metadata.title: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU): Agronomic Efficacy and Preparation of Panchagavya
metadata.author: Department of Sustainable Organic Agriculture, TNAU, Coimbatore

chunks.content:
3. STEP-BY-STEP PROTOCOL
- Phase 1 (Days 1 to 3): Place 5 kg cow dung and 1 kg cow ghee in a wide-mouth plastic/clay container. Mix thoroughly into a homogenous paste. Let it stand for 3 days. Stir clockwise once daily. This anaerobic initial phase breaks down fatty layers.
- Phase 2 (Day 4): Add 3 liters cow urine, 10 liters water (if needed), and mix well. Allow standing for 24 hours.
- Phase 3 (Day 5 onwards): Add 2 liters cow milk, 2 liters cow curd, 3 liters tender coconut water, jaggery syrup, and 12 mashed bananas. Mix thoroughly.

metadata.title: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU): Agronomic Efficacy and Preparation of Panchagavya
metadata.author: Department of Sustainable Organic Agriculture, TNAU, Coimbatore

chunks.content:
- Stirring Routine: Stir the mixture clockwise for 10 minutes in the morning and 10 minutes in the evening daily for 15 to 18 days. Keep container covered with a mosquito mesh or muslin cloth under cool shade.
- Ready State: On the 18th day, a pleasant fruity alcoholic aroma develops with no foul stench. Filter through nylon mesh for spraying.

metadata.title: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU): Agronomic Efficacy and Preparation of Panchagavya
metadata.author: Department of Sustainable Organic Agriculture, TNAU, Coimbatore

chunks.content:
4. APPLICATION RATES AND FIELD DOSAGES
- Foliar Spray (Standard): 3% solution (300 ml Panchagavya mixed in 10 liters of clean water, equivalent to 6 liters in 200 liters water per acre).
- Flow with Irrigation / Fertigation: 20 to 50 liters per acre mixed in irrigation water.
- Seed / Seedling Treatment: 3% solution dip for 20 minutes before sowing or transplanting. Enhances seed germination vigor by 28-35%.
- Storage of Rhizomes / Tubers (Turmeric, Ginger, Potato): Dip seed rhizomes in 3% solution for 30 minutes before storage to suppress rot pathogens.

metadata.title: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU): Agronomic Efficacy and Preparation of Panchagavya
metadata.author: Department of Sustainable Organic Agriculture, TNAU, Coimbatore

chunks.content:
5. SCIENTIFIC BENEFIT HIGHLIGHTS
- Significant increase in leaf chlorophyll index, canopy surface area, and branch branching.
- Induces synchronous profuse flowering and reduces premature flower and fruit drop by 40%.
- Systemic acquired resistance (SAR) against fungal powdery mildews and viral symptoms.

metadata.title: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU): Agronomic Efficacy and Preparation of Panchagavya
metadata.author: Department of Sustainable Organic Agriculture, TNAU, Coimbatore

chunks.content:
1. INSECT PEST COMPLEX OF COTTON IN INDIA
Organic cotton cultivation requires preemptive biological and ecological management against two major pest groups:
- Sucking Pests (Vegetative Phase, 15 to 60 DAS): Jassids (Amrasca biguttula), Aphids (Aphis gossypii), Thrips (Thrips tabaci), Whitefly (Bemisia tabaci).
- Bollworm Complex (Squaring & Boll Formation Phase, 60 to 120 DAS): American bollworm (Helicoverpa armigera), Spotted bollworm (Earias vittella), Pink bollworm (Pectinophora gossypiella).

metadata.title: ICAR-Central Institute for Cotton Research: Organic Integrated Pest Management (IPM) in Cotton
metadata.author: ICAR-Central Institute for Cotton Research (CICR), Nagpur

chunks.content:
2. AGRO-ECOSYSTEM DIVERSITY & BORDER CROPPING
- Border Trap Cropping: Plant 2 to 3 dense border rows of Maize (Zea mays) or Sorghum (Jowar) around the entire cotton perimeter. Serves as a physical wind barrier against whitefly migrations and provides refuge for predatory pirate bugs (Orius spp.) and Ladybird beetles (Coccinella septempunctata).
- Intercropping: Plant 1 row of Pigeonpea (Arhar) or Cowpea (Lobia) after every 4 to 5 rows of cotton. Cowpea attracts beneficial predatory insects; Marigold (Tagetes erecta) planted as trap crop attracts Helicoverpa armigera egg laying away from cotton bolls.

metadata.title: ICAR-Central Institute for Cotton Research: Organic Integrated Pest Management (IPM) in Cotton
metadata.author: ICAR-Central Institute for Cotton Research (CICR), Nagpur

chunks.content:
3. MONITORING AND PHEROMONE TRAPPING
- Trap Installation: Install sleeve pheromone traps with Gossyplure (for Pink bollworm) and Helilure (for American bollworm) @ 5 traps per acre at 45 days after sowing. Place traps 1 foot above the top crop canopy.
- Action Threshold (ETL):
  * Pink bollworm: 8 male moths caught per trap per night for 3 consecutive nights, or 10% damaged green bolls (with rosette flowers).
  * Jassids: 1-2 nymphs per leaf on top leaves.
  * Whitefly: 6-8 adults per leaf.
- Mass Trapping: Increase trap density to 10-12 traps per acre when moth influx is observed.

metadata.title: ICAR-Central Institute for Cotton Research: Organic Integrated Pest Management (IPM) in Cotton
metadata.author: ICAR-Central Institute for Cotton Research (CICR), Nagpur

chunks.content:
4. BIO-CONTROL AGENTS AND PARASITOIDS
- Trichogramma chilonis Egg Parasitoid: Release Trichocards @ 60,000 eggs (3 to 4 cards) per acre per week, starting from 45 DAS for 4-5 releases. Parasitizes bollworm eggs within 24 hours, preventing larval emergence.
- Chrysoperla carnea (Green lacewing): Release 1st instar larvae @ 4,000 to 5,000 per acre to predate upon aphids, thrips, and young bollworm larvae.
- Entomopathogens: Spray Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt var. kurstaki) @ 400 g/acre or HaNPV (Helicoverpa Nuclear Polyhedrosis Virus) @ 250 LE/acre with 0.1% jaggery sticker in evening hours against Helicoverpa.

metadata.title: ICAR-Central Institute for Cotton Research: Organic Integrated Pest Management (IPM) in Cotton
metadata.author: ICAR-Central Institute for Cotton Research (CICR), Nagpur

chunks.content:
5. BOTANICAL AND INDIGENOUS PREPARATIONS
- Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE 5%): Grind 5 kg shade-dried neem seeds, soak in 10 liters water overnight with 200 g soap powder, filter, dilute to 100 liters water, and spray immediately. Disrupts insect oviposition and acts as antifeedant.
- Cold-pressed Neem Oil: Use 1500 ppm or 3000 ppm neem oil @ 5 ml per liter of water with 1 ml organic liquid detergent/soapnut solution as emulsifier.
- Agniastra / Dashaparni Ark: Decoction of neem leaves, karanj leaves, vitex leaves, chilli paste, garlic paste boiled in cow urine. Highly effective against resistant sucking pest colonies.

metadata.title: ICAR-Central Institute for Cotton Research: Organic Integrated Pest Management (IPM) in Cotton
metadata.author: ICAR-Central Institute for Cotton Research (CICR), Nagpur

chunks.content:
1. COMMON DISEASES AND ORGANIC DIAGNOSTIC CRITERIA
- Early Blight (Alternaria solani): Concentric target-board ring brown lesions on older leaves, progressing upward; stem lesions leading to collar rot.
- Late Blight (Phytophthora infestans): Water-soaked dark brown irregular lesions on foliage and greenish-brown firm rot on fruit under cool humid conditions (>90% RH, 18-22°C).
- Bacterial Wilt (Ralstonia solanacearum): Sudden daytime wilting of plant without foliage yellowing. Stems show vascular browning; stem-cut water streaming test emits milky bacterial streaming.
- Tomato Leaf Curl Virus (ToLCV): Severe leaf curling, puckering, stunting, and bushy appearance transmitted by silverleaf whitefly (Bemisia tabaci).

metadata.title: ICAR-IIHR: Package of Practices for Organic Tomato Cultivation and Disease Management
metadata.author: Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (ICAR-IIHR), Bengaluru

chunks.content:
2. SOIL & NURSERY PREPARATION
- Soil Solarization: Cover moist nursery raised beds with 25-micron transparent UV-stabilized polyethylene sheets for 30 to 45 days in peak summer (April-May). Elevated soil temperature (up to 55°C) kills resting sclerotia, nematodes, and fungal propagules.
- Trichoderma Seed Treatment: Treat certified organic seeds with Trichoderma viride or T. harzianum @ 10 g per kg seed + Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10 g per kg seed. Reduces damping-off by 85%.
- Arka Microbial Consortium (AMC): Enrich 1 tonne of farmyard manure or vermicompost with 5 kg IIHR Arka Microbial Consortium (containing N-fixers, P-solubilizers, K-solubilizers, and Trichoderma), maintain moisture under shade for 15 days, and apply in furrows.

metadata.title: ICAR-IIHR: Package of Practices for Organic Tomato Cultivation and Disease Management
metadata.author: Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (ICAR-IIHR), Bengaluru

chunks.content:
3. CULTURAL PREVENTIVE PRACTICES
- Spacing & Staking: Transplant at 75 cm row-to-row and 60 cm plant-to-plant spacing. Strict staking with bamboo stakes or trellis wires keeps foliage 2 feet above ground, preventing splash dispersal of fungal spores.
- De-suckering and Lower Leaf Pruning: Remove all bottom leaves touching the soil surface up to 30 cm height at 45 days after transplanting to maximize air circulation.
- Organic Mulching: Spread 4-5 inches of dry paddy straw, sugarcane bagasse, or coconut coir mulch to prevent soil splashing during irrigation/rain.

metadata.title: ICAR-IIHR: Package of Practices for Organic Tomato Cultivation and Disease Management
metadata.author: Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (ICAR-IIHR), Bengaluru

chunks.content:
4. BIO-FUNGICIDE AND INDIGENOUS MANAGEMENT SPRAYS
- Sour Buttermilk (Khatti Chhachh) Spray: Ferment fresh cow buttermilk in an earthen pot with a copper plate/wire for 7 to 10 days. Dilute 50 ml fermented buttermilk per liter of water (5% concentration) and spray at 10-day intervals. Lactic acid and cuprous bio-chelates suppress Alternaria early blight and Powdery Mildew.
- Pseudomonas fluorescens: Spray @ 5 g per liter or 1 kg per acre in 200 liters water. Colonizes leaf phyllosphere and secretes phenazine antibiotics against early fungal infections.
- Yellow Sticky Traps: Install 15-20 bright yellow sticky sheets per acre at canopy height to capture whiteflies and mitigate Tomato Leaf Curl Virus incidence.

metadata.title: ICAR-IIHR: Package of Practices for Organic Tomato Cultivation and Disease Management
metadata.author: Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (ICAR-IIHR), Bengaluru

chunks.content: - Copper Oxychloride Alternative: For emergency rescue in certified organic farming, use approved copper hydroxide/Bordeaux mixture (1%) only as allowed by NPOP standards when fungal blights threaten complete crop loss.

metadata.title: ICAR-IIHR: Package of Practices for Organic Tomato Cultivation and Disease Management
metadata.author: Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (ICAR-IIHR), Bengaluru

chunks.content:
1. VARIETAL SUITABILITY FOR ORGANIC RICE
Traditional tall and aromatic cultivars perform exceptionally well under organic regimes due to deep rooting, nutrient efficiency, and native pest resistance:
- BPT-5204 (Samba Mahsuri - organic management), RNR-15048 (Telangana Sona - low glycemic index), Kalanamak, Indrayani, Gobindobhog, Navara, Karuppu Kavuni, and Ratnachodi.

metadata.title: ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research: Comprehensive Organic Package of Practices for Rice/Paddy
metadata.author: ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research (ICAR-IIRR), Rajendranagar, Hyderabad

chunks.content:
2. GREEN MANURING AND SOIL ENRICHMENT
- Pre-season Sowing: Broadcast Dhaincha (Sesbania aculeata) or Sunnhemp (Crotalaria juncea) seeds @ 15 to 20 kg per acre immediately after summer pre-monsoon showers.
- Incorporation: At 45 to 50 days (50% flowering stage), when plant tissue is succulent and nitrogen-rich, plough and incorporate the biomass into the puddled field using a disc plough or rotavator. Adds 8 to 12 tonnes of green biomass and 60 to 75 kg organic Nitrogen per acre.
- Allow 10-12 days for decomposition under submerged conditions before transplanting rice seedlings.

metadata.title: ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research: Comprehensive Organic Package of Practices for Rice/Paddy
metadata.author: ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research (ICAR-IIRR), Rajendranagar, Hyderabad

chunks.content:
3. SRI (SYSTEM OF RICE INTENSIFICATION) ORGANIC TRANSPLANTING
- Seedling Age: Transplant very young seedlings (8 to 12 days old, 2-leaf stage) with seed and root intact.
- Spacing: Single seedling per hill at a wide square grid of 25 cm x 25 cm.
- Bio-treatment: Dip seedling roots in a slurry of Azospirillum (1 kg) + PSB (1 kg) + Pseudomonas fluorescens (1 kg) in 40 liters water for 30 minutes before planting.

metadata.title: ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research: Comprehensive Organic Package of Practices for Rice/Paddy
metadata.author: ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research (ICAR-IIRR), Rajendranagar, Hyderabad

chunks.content:
4. ORGANIC NUTRIENT SCHEDULE (PER ACRE)
- Basal Application: 2.5 tonnes of well-rotted Farmyard Manure or 1.5 tonnes of enriched Vermicompost + 200 kg Neem Cake (suppresses root-knot nematodes and retards nitrogen leaching).
- At Active Tillering (20-25 DAT): Apply 200 liters of Jeevamrutham through irrigation channel + broadcast Azolla pinnata @ 200 to 400 kg per acre. Azolla forms a thick floating carpet, suppresses weeds, and fixes 30 kg atmospheric N per acre when incorporated during cono-weeding.
- Panicle Initiation (45-50 DAT): Spray Panchagavya 3% (300 ml in 10 liters water) + 200 liters Jeevamrutham in irrigation.

metadata.title: ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research: Comprehensive Organic Package of Practices for Rice/Paddy
metadata.author: ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research (ICAR-IIRR), Rajendranagar, Hyderabad

chunks.content:
- Flowering / Milk Stage (70-75 DAT): Foliar spray of 5% fermented buttermilk + 3% Panchagavya to improve grain filling and mitigate sheath rot.

5. WEED & WATER MANAGEMENT
- Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD): Do not keep paddy flooded continuously with 5-10 cm water. Keep soil saturated to thin water film (1-2 cm), allowing hair-cracking before next irrigation. Reduces methane emissions by 40% and stimulates deep root aeration.
- Mechanical Cono-Weeding: Operate mechanical cono-weeder at 15, 25, and 35 days after transplanting between the 25 cm grid rows. Buries weeds into soil as in-situ green manure and aerates root rhizosphere.

metadata.title: ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research: Comprehensive Organic Package of Practices for Rice/Paddy
metadata.author: ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research (ICAR-IIRR), Rajendranagar, Hyderabad

chunks.content:
1. CLASSIFICATION OF AGRICULTURAL BIOFERTILIZERS
Biofertilizers are living carrier-based microbial preparations that enrich soil biological fertility through nitrogen fixation, phosphorus solubilization, or mycorrhizal mobilization:
- Nitrogen-Fixing Biofertilizers:
  * Rhizobium: Symbiotic N-fixer specifically compatible with legume nodules. Specific strains: R. leguminosarum (pea, lentil), R. phaseoli (beans), R. japonicum (soybean), Bradyrhizobium (cowpea, groundnut). Fixes 50 to 150 kg N/ha.
  * Azotobacter chroococcum: Free-living aerobic N-fixer for non-leguminous upland crops (wheat, cotton, maize, vegetables). Fixes 20-30 kg N/ha and synthesizes gibberellic acid.

metadata.title: National Centre for Organic Farming: Biofertilizers and Green Manuring for Regenerative Soil Health
metadata.author: National Centre for Organic and Natural Farming, MoA&FW, Government of India

chunks.content:
* Azospirillum brasilense: Associative symbiotic bacterium for cereals, grasses, sugarcane, and paddy. Fixes 20-40 kg N/ha.
  * Blue-Green Algae (BGA / Cyanobacteria - Anabaena azollae): Specialized for wetland paddy ecosystems.
- Phosphorus Solubilizing Biofertilizers (PSB):
  * Bacillus megaterium var. phosphaticum, Pseudomonas putida, Aspergillus awamori. Secretes citric, oxalic, and malic acids that break calcium-phosphate and iron-phosphate bonds in neutral/alkaline Indian soils, releasing 30-50 kg bio-available P2O5 per hectare.
- Potassium & Zinc Mobilizing Microorganisms:
  * Frateuria aurantia (Potash mobilizer) and Thiobacillus / Bacillus zinc solubilizers.

metadata.title: National Centre for Organic Farming: Biofertilizers and Green Manuring for Regenerative Soil Health
metadata.author: National Centre for Organic and Natural Farming, MoA&FW, Government of India

chunks.content:
2. GREEN MANURING SPECIES & REGENERATIVE METRICS
- Sesbania aculeata (Dhaincha): Highly adapted to saline, sodic, and waterlogged soils. Biomass yield: 20-25 tonnes/ha in 45 days. Nitrogen contribution: 80-100 kg N/ha.
- Crotalaria juncea (Sunnhemp): Excellent for well-drained loamy and sandy soils. Fast initial growth; incorporates within 40-45 days. Also suppresses root-knot nematodes through pyrrolizidine alkaloid exudates.
- Sesbania rostrata: Stem-nodulating species that fixes nitrogen even under complete submergence.

metadata.title: National Centre for Organic Farming: Biofertilizers and Green Manuring for Regenerative Soil Health
metadata.author: National Centre for Organic and Natural Farming, MoA&FW, Government of India

chunks.content:
3. CARRIER APPLICATION TECHNIQUES
- Seed Treatment (Beejamrutham / Slurry method): Mix 250 g biofertilizer carrier powder with 200 ml cooled 10% jaggery solution to form a sticky adhesive. Coat 10 kg seeds gently without rupturing seed coat. Dry in shade for 30 minutes before immediate sowing.
- Soil Application: Mix 2 to 3 kg of carrier biofertilizer per acre with 200 kg moist vermicompost or well-decomposed FYM. Broadcast uniformly over field before sowing or during hoeing.
- Root Dip for Transplants: Suspend 1 kg biofertilizer in 40 liters clean water. Dip seedling root cluster for 20-30 minutes before planting in main field.

metadata.title: National Centre for Organic Farming: Biofertilizers and Green Manuring for Regenerative Soil Health
metadata.author: National Centre for Organic and Natural Farming, MoA&FW, Government of India
